scenes.voice: An index makes reads fast. But it quietly makes every write slower.
An index is a sorted lookup structure. The database can jump to your row instead of scanning the whole table.
Without one, a lookup on a big table reads every row. With one, the database finds the row directly.
But every insert, update, and delete must also update each index. More indexes means more write work, and more disk.
So index the columns you filter and join on often. Skip the rest, and check with explain.
scenes.code:
EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM users
WHERE email = 'a@b.com';

scenes.voice: Index for the reads you actually have. Save this for the next time a query is slow.
